findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated at runtime
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement any of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). If a Detector with type 'metric_alert_fire' is created and its `detector_handler` property is accessed, the call `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in `Detector.detector_handler` will raise a TypeError ('Can't instantiate abstract class...') that is not caught, crashing the request. Even though this is marked as a TODO placeholder, the MetricAlertFire GroupType is registered and references this handler, making the crash reachable.

findings.title: Docstring still says 'returns a list' after changing return type to dict
findings.body: The docstring for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` reads 'Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`' but the method now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. This should be updated to say 'returns a dict' to avoid confusing future readers.

findings.title: Test passes incorrect value (6 instead of 10) for group_2 occurrence construction
findings.body: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, the data packet contains `{'group_1': 6, 'group_2': 10}`, but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, 'group_2', 6, ...)` using value 6 instead of 10. The actual code path in `evaluate_group_key_value` passes the real value from the packet to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. The test passes only because the mock helper ignores the `value` parameter, but this means the test does not verify that the correct value is threaded through, and it will silently produce wrong expectations if the implementation ever uses the value.
